subject: QBR alignment: usage review, OKR touchpoints, and decision lanes
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acmedata.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmedata.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR: request for usage & SLO review ahead of next week

Hi Vivek,

Hope youre well. Were putting together our internal materials for the QBR and want to make sure the agenda covers a couple of things that are top of mind for our execs:

- Verified monthly usage trends (top 3 inference workloads, percent of total tokens by workload)
- Current SLO attainment and any incidents in the quarter that affected latency or error rates
- Any planned capacity/upgrade changes that would affect our forecast for next quarter

Would you be able to share a short packet (1-2 slides) and availability for a 45-minute sync the week of July 20? Procurement also wants to review the latest SOW and any open terms. If you can include a draft we can circulate, that would be helpful.

Thanks, and happy to be flexible on time.

—Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Data Platform, Acme Data
jordan.mills@acmedata.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.mills@acmedata.com, procurement@acmedata.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: QBR: request for usage & SLO review ahead of next week

Team — looping you in for a quick internal alignment before we send back the Acme packet. High level plan:

1) Deliverable to Acme: 2-slide summary (usage + SLO + 3 prioritized asks), proposed 45-min agenda, and the latest SOW draft.
2) Internal owners: Marcus — usage numbers + trend bullets; Dylan — incident summary & SLO attainment; Laura — executive framing and ask lanes. Ill own the proposed agenda and final packet assembly.
3) Timing: Id like a short internal sync Wednesday 7/15 at 11:00 PT (30 min) to finalize. If that works, Ill assemble the packet and send to Jordan by EOD Friday 7/17 so Acme can prep before the week of 7/20.

Quick notes on what we should surface in the packet (draft bullets):
- Wins: sustained 99.8% query success for primary model (vs 99.2% last quarter); 18% reduction in avg latency after latest kernel update.
- Risks: forecasted token spike from Acmes batch migration (expected mid-Aug), margin pressure if batching not tuned; one open infra risk (node OS upgrade window) that could require a brief maintenance window.
- Asks: commit to a targeted burst capacity configuration for 6 weeks; acceptance of revised data-retention clause in SOW; a mutual action plan checkpoint after 30 days.

Attachments I will include in the outgoing: QBR-agenda-v2.pdf (agenda + time-boxed topics) and SOW-draft.docx (with redlines). Put any reference docs in the shared drive link below.

If Wednesday 11:00 PT works, Ill send a calendar invite and draft packet before the sync.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer-Facing Ops | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: QBR: request for usage & SLO review ahead of next week

Thanks Vivek — 11:00 PT works for me. I pulled together a compact wins/risks/asks note to prime the packet. See below; happy to iterate in the sync.

Wins (quick bullets for slide 1)
- Core inference pipeline: 18% lower p95 latency quarter-over-quarter after kernel selection update.
- Cache effectiveness: prefix/KV caching cut token usage for recurrent workloads by ~12% for Acme's top two jobs.
- Reliability: no customer-impacting incidents in June; only degraded performance alert triggered twice (both mitigated).

Risks (to call out, one-line each)
- Batch migration (Acme): potential 30–40% token increase in peak windows if batching profiles not tuned.
- OS upgrade window: scheduled maintenance could push a 2–3 hour risk window if coordination slips.
- SOW term: Acme legal flagged data-retention language; procurement will want a narrower clause.

Asks (what we need from Acme/leadership)
- Approval to enable 6-week burst pool during migration (estimate cost delta attached).
- Sign-off on revised section 4 (data retention) with mutual audit language.
- Agreement on a 30-day post-migration review (mutual action plan owner: Acme PM + Redwood CS).

Ive also added two short speaker notes for the meeting: 1) Open with the 60-second health snapshot; 2) Move quickly to the migration impact scenarios and recommended mitigations.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

[Attachment stub: cost-estimate-burst-pool.xlsx (referenced)]

Jordan — thanks for the ask and patience. Sending our proposed 45-minute agenda and a short two-slide packet attached (QBR-agenda-v2.pdf). Also attached is the current SOW draft with the redlines we discussed (SOW-draft.docx).

Proposed agenda (45 minutes):
- 0:00–5:00 — Quick health snapshot (Laura)
- 5:00–15:00 — Usage trends & migration forecast (Marcus)
- 15:00–25:00 — SLO and incident recap (Dylan)
- 25:00–35:00 — Migration impact scenarios + recommended mitigations (Vivek)
- 35:00–45:00 — Decisions & next steps (mutual action plan owner assignment)

Key asks were proposing to surface in the meeting:
- Approval for a 6-week burst capacity during migration (weve provided cost estimate separately).
- Agreement on the revised data-retention clause proposed in the SOW (see redlines).
- Confirm mutual action plan cadence: 30-day checkpoint after migration completes.

Can we do Tuesday 7/21 at 10:00 PT for the presentation? If that slot doesnt work, propose alternatives and well adjust. Once you confirm, well calendarize and include folks from infra/procurement as needed.

Best,
Vivek
VP, Customer-Facing Ops | Redwood Inference
